title: Yield curves for zero-coupon bonds
summary: The Bank of Canada publishes daily zero-coupon yield curve data for Government of Canada bonds and treasury bills, with terms to maturity ranging from 0.25 years to 30 years. Data are expressed as decimals and updated each Thursday by 16:30 ET with a two-week lag.
key_points: Zero-coupon yield curves are generated using pricing data for Government of Canada bonds and treasury bills
Maturity terms range from 0.25 years (3 months) to 30.00 years (column 1 to column 120)
Data are updated each Thursday by 16:30 ET with a two-week lag
Methodology is described in Bolder, Johnson, and Metzler (2004) paper on Canadian term structure
Missing data due to holidays or data problems are shown as 'na'
why_it_matters: This page provides access to benchmark Canadian interest rate data across the full maturity spectrum. The shape and level of the zero-coupon yield curve are key inputs for macro forecasting, fixed income valuation, and policy signal extraction. However, the page itself is a data portal rather than analytical content.
macro_context: Zero-coupon yield curve data are fundamental macro inputs used to gauge term premiums, growth expectations, and monetary policy stance. The Bank of Canada's weekly update schedule with two-week lag means data are not real-time.
